note: Attacker-controlled first byte (0x03) selects the logfmt parser format.
When the types_str branch is taken (byte 0x05), five parser types are registered; key "CCC" is assigned FLB_PARSER_TYPE_BOOL.
Parser is created with types_len=5, so typecasting is enabled for parsed keys.
Remaining attacker-controlled bytes (log line ending in 'CCC=x') are passed to the parser; 'x' is the final byte of the 107-byte heap input buffer.
Dispatch to the logfmt parser based on the selected format.

code: flb_parser_typecast((const char*) key, key_len, (const char*) value, value_len, ...);
note: Parses pair 'CCC=x'; value points to 'x' at the very end of the buffer with value_len=1, and key 'CCC' is not null-terminated. Because types_len != 0, typecast is invoked.

code: if (!strncasecmp(val, "true", 4)) { ... else if(!strncasecmp(val, "false", 5)){ ... } else { error = FLB_TRUE; }
note: val_len is 1, so 'x' matches neither "true" nor "false"; the BOOL cast fails and error is set to FLB_TRUE.

code: flb_warn("[PARSER] key=%s cast error. save as string.", key);
note: key points into the input buffer and is not null-terminated; printf reads it as %s past the end of the 107-byte heap region -> heap-buffer-overflow READ (confirmed by ASAN at flb_parser.c:917).
